I will stay with the wheat-maize rotation on all of my land this year. In Quzhou County, that is the steadiest way for me to keep grain output, use the land fully for the whole year, and avoid taking on extra market risk. At my age and with the way I farm, I would rather choose a familiar system I know how to manage well than chase a crop with higher upside but more uncertainty. I will plant winter wheat first with an improved variety because it is reliable, handles local conditions better, and gives me stable yield if I keep fertilizer and water on time. After wheat harvest, I will go straight into summer maize with a hybrid seed because maize responds well here and fits the season tightly. I will keep fertilizer moderate instead of excessive, because too much input raises cost and can lodge the crop or waste money. I will irrigate wheat more than maize because wheat in our area depends more on timely water, especially around jointing and grain filling. I will use pesticides only as needed but I know I will still need a couple of sprays for weeds, aphids, and common disease pressure. For tillage, I will use rotary tillage for wheat because it gives me a clean seedbed, and I will use no-tillage for summer maize after wheat so I can save time, hold moisture, and get the maize in quickly.
